articleSummary: ALTNV, a novel virus linked to the Asian longhorned tick (Haemaphysalis longicornis), was detected in China in patients with influenza-like illness who tested negative for DBV. ALTNV alone did not show higher mortality, but co-infection with both viruses correlated with more respiratory symptoms and kidney dysfunction, with seven deaths among co-infected individuals. The Asian longhorned tick, established in the United States since 2017, has spread to more than 20 states and reproduces asexually, aiding expansion. It remains unknown whether US ticks transmit ALTNV to humans; tick-borne transmission depends on animals carrying the pathogen. The Chinese finding raises concerns about cross-border spread and the tick’s capacity to carry multiple pathogens, including implications for livestock health due to parasite transmission.

articleSummary: Anthrax outbreak in eastern Zambia’s Munyamadzi Reserve with 12 human cases after consuming meat from wild animals found near the river. Affected individuals are receiving treatment; investigations are ongoing in the field and laboratory, and security teams have been deployed to secure carcasses and deter poaching around the reserve. Residents are urged to report any dead wildlife and avoid handling carcasses. Transmission is Bacillus anthracis, which persists in soil; humans are typically infected via contaminated animal products, and this event’s infections are linked to eating wild game meat. Geographic spread is not yet defined as studies continue.

articleSummary: El Tor cholera outbreak among Indonesian Haj pilgrims spurred the creation of Indonesia’s first Hajj Dormitory, Pondok Gede, in East Jakarta. Saudi medical checks found El Tor cholera among pilgrims from Sulawesi, prompting mandatory quarantine before entering the haram. In 1970, WHO designated Indonesia as affected by El Tor cholera, leading to a quarantine regime of five days before departure and five days after return (later shortened to three days pre- and post-travel in 1973). To avoid rising rental costs for temporary quarantine spaces amid shifting air travel, the government planned a permanent facility: SP-08/1974 established the Hajj Quarantine Dormitory Planning Team. About 15 hectares were allocated in Jalan Raya Pondok Gede, Pinang Ranti, Makasar, Jakarta Timur, in 1977; construction 1978–1979; officially opened in 1979. Governance moved from Proyek Asrama Haji to BPAH (1982), and since 2014 to UPT Asrama Haji Embarkasi Jakarta under the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah. Today the complex serves as a multifunction public space for education, worship, and UMKM.

articleSummary: An Italian travel-associated tick bite in a Chinese woman progressed to severe neurological symptoms after returning home, prompting suspicion of Lyme disease. Diagnosis cannot be made from symptoms alone; pathogen detection and laboratory confirmation are required. The case is overseas-imported, with potential pathogen strains different from domestic ones, underscoring the need for etiological testing. Lyme disease often starts with erythema migrans at the bite site, then weeks later can involve meningitis, encephalitis, neuropathy, or carditis. Preventive measures include prompt tick removal, protective clothing in wooded areas, checking for ticks after outdoor activity, and using heat to kill ticks on clothing.

articleSummary: Two Hanoi-area scrub typhus cases (Orientia tsutsugamushi) are described. Eschar—a necrotic, often painless lesion—can appear in hidden sites like the armpit, groin, under the breast, or genitals. Not all cases have eschar. Without early treatment, scrub typhus can progress to pneumonia, respiratory failure, liver/kidney injury, coagulopathy, multi-organ failure, or death; early doxycycline is effective.

Preventive measures include waterproofing, protective footwear, masks, boiled water, and thorough hand hygiene.

articleSummary: Mpox multi-country outbreak remains ongoing with health risk rated moderate in August 2026. A mpox vaccine access initiative was launched on 27 August 2026 in Addis Ababa under the ICG to support vaccine provision. July 2026, 32 countries in four WHO regions reported 1,370 mpox cases and 7 deaths (CFR 0.5%), about 75% in Africa; Madagascar, Angola, China, DRC and Kenya reported most. Eleven African countries had active transmission in the prior six weeks (6 Jul–16 Aug 2026): 1,153 confirmed cases and 7 deaths (CFR 0.6%), led by Madagascar, Angola, Kenya, DRC and Cameroon. Transmission remains largely sexual, with all MPXV clades circulating; Chile and Hungary reported mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time. Eastern Mediterranean Region reported no confirmed cases in July.

articleHeadline: RDC-Ebola: 6 zones de santé franchissent 42 jours sans nouveau cas, 4 autres dépassent 21 jours
articleSummary: Six health zones in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have had no new Ebola cases for more than 42 days, and four others surpassed 21 days, according to Health Minister Roger Kamba. In total, 62 zones have reported at least one Ebola case since the outbreak began, including a zone in Sud-Ubangi; 52 zones remain with active transmission. The 21-day and 42-day thresholds mark Ebola’s incubation windows and two cycles. Daily cases have fallen from about 120 at the peak to around 80; daily deaths from roughly 50 to 30. The reproductive number is about 0.9, down from peaks of 1.2–2. An imported case has been confirmed in Sud-Ubangi: a 23-year-old man from South Kivu who traveled through Rwanda and Uganda and died in a Sud-Ubangi health center. The outbreak is under control but not over; 10 zones have had no cases for at least 21 days.
